s2.ptxt: Release Lock Pin

s3.ptxt: Cover the 4 oil holes in the cam journal with vinyl tape, etc. as shown in the illustration.

atten4.ptxt: 4 of the oil holes are inside the groove, so plug only 2 of them using a piece of rubber, etc.

s3.ptxt: Make holes in the vinyl tape covering the 2 oil holes (advance oil hole, retard oil hole) on the opposite side.
To the 2 oil holes (advance oil hole, retard oil hole) where holes were made in the vinyl tape, 200kPa{2.0kgf/cm2apply air pressure of approximately }.

atten3.ptxt: When applying air pressure, oil may splash, so cover with a shop rag, etc.

s3.ptxt: From the above condition, gradually reduce the air pressure on the retard oil hole side and check that the camshaft timing gear assembly rotates in the advance direction.

atten4.ptxt: The lock pin is released and the gear rotates in the advance direction.

s3.ptxt: When the camshaft timing gear assembly reaches the most advanced position, release the air pressure on the retard oil hole side, and then release the air pressure on the advance oil hole side.

atten3.ptxt: If the air pressure on the advance oil hole side is released first, the camshaft timing gear assembly may move suddenly in the retard direction and damage the lock pin, etc., so always release the air pressure on the retard oil hole side first.

s2.ptxt: Check Movement

s3.ptxt: Move the camshaft timing gear assembly back and forth 2-3 times within the movable range [21°] excluding the most retarded position, and check that it moves smoothly.

atten3.ptxt: Do not check the movement by applying air pressure; always do it by hand.
